# single-h1

- ID: `MD025`
- Category: Headings
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: no
- Tags: `headings`
- Also named: `single-title`, as in markdownlint

A document that starts with a title has no other top-level heading.

## Why

The top-level heading at the start is the document's title, and a document has
only one title.

## Options

Set them under `rules.single-h1.options`.

- `level` (`integer`, default `1`): Level of the title heading.
- `front_matter_title` (`string|false`, default `^\s*"?title"?\s*[:=]`): Regular
  expression, matched in any case, for the front matter line that gives the
  document a title, which counts as the title, so every heading of the title's
  level is reported. An empty string or false turns this off.
- `title_only` (`boolean`, default `true`, gomdlint only): Report more title
  headings only when the first one is the document's title, its first content.
  With false, every title heading after the first is reported.
- `allow_no_h1` (`boolean`, default `true`, gomdlint only): Allow a document
  without a title heading. With false, such a document is reported.

## Fix

There is no automatic fix. Only the author knows which heading should stay the
title.

## Example

This document breaks the rule:

```markdown
# Guide

Install the tool.

# Usage

Run it in the project root.
```

gomdlint reports:

```text
5:1 Multiple H1 headings found (this is H1 #2)
```

This document follows the rule:

```markdown
# Guide

Install the tool.

## Usage

Run it in the project root.
```

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  single-h1:
    options:
      level: 1
```

Under `rules`, `single-h1: false` turns the rule off and `single-h1: error`
reports its findings as errors. The flag `--disable single-h1` turns it off for
one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line single-title -->
```
